checks.what: Setup, hold and pulse-width slack must be met after routing, and no endpoint may be left unconstrained.

Checks design.xdc: clocks only on the board's clock input, no disabled clock-route check, a reason beside every false path or asynchronous clock group. Run as the check_constraints tool; a command outside the allow-list refuses the build.
Applies the exceptions that AMD ships as scoped files for its crossing macros, which the batch flow otherwise drops.

After synthesis and after routing: no exception ignored or covering no path, no constraint message from an XDC line, no TIMING-24/-29/-47 or XDCH-1, and every multicycle path's registers share a real clock enable.
Before Vivado: a -setup N multicycle needs its -hold N-1, and a multicycle or datapath-only max delay needs a comment naming the enable or the synchroniser.

evidence.text: On 10 small designs with one timing-exception mistake each, Vivado itself said something about the exception in 5; the flow's checks flagged 10. They passed 4 of 4 correct designs.
On a two-clock probe design, setup slack on the crossing was -1.364 ns without the macro exceptions and 8.891 ns with them (Vivado 2025.2).
16 development runs reached routing and recorded post-route setup slack; it was positive in 16.

gaps: Exceptions that hide a real failure (a blanket false path, a clock group over a failing path) are designed as tasks but not built or run; Brief 20 settles this.
I/O delay constraints are written from skills; no committed run scores them against a data sheet.
